note: Influence and approval are gameplay starting values for 1 January 2000 (Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, reformist President Khatami, conservative-led 5th Majlis), not measured data. Influence reflects institutional weight: the clergy and the security apparatus (Revolutionary Guards, Basij, intelligence) answer to the Supreme Leader, independent unions are weak, and the reformist press and student movement were at a high point.

interest_groups.note: Regular army (Artesh) and Revolutionary Guards; both under the Supreme Leader's command.
Revolutionary Guards, Basij and intelligence services, generally aligned with the principlist camp rather than the reformist government.
Bazaar merchants (close to the Islamic Coalition Party) and large state-linked foundations.
No independent unions; officially sanctioned labour bodies.
Clergy divided between the CCA (principlist) and the ACC (reformist).
Ethnic minorities (Azerbaijanis, Kurds, Arabs, Baloch and others) and the recognised religious minorities with five reserved Majlis seats.
Student organisations were a pillar of the 2nd of Khordad movement.
A large reformist print press alongside state broadcasting controlled by the Supreme Leader's appointee.
